title: The Bunyakovsky–Schwarz Bridge beyond L²: Hölder's Inequality

meta.author: Lean Genius
meta.assumptions: None beyond the per-theorem hypotheses that the functions lie in the relevant Lᵖ / Lᵍ spaces (MemLp), which are part of the statements rather than global axioms. Fully machine-verified: #print axioms reports only the foundational propext / Classical.choice / Quot.sound.
originalContributions: holder_integral_abs: the signed Hölder integral inequality |∫ f·g dμ| ≤ (∫ |f|ᵖ)^{1/p}·(∫ |g|ᵍ)^{1/q} for real-valued f ∈ Lᵖ, g ∈ Lᵍ with conjugate exponents — Mathlib ships only the nonnegative form (integral_mul_le_Lp_mul_Lq_of_nonneg) and the norm form (integral_mul_norm_le_Lp_mul_Lq); bounding the signed pairing directly is the genuine generalization of the parent's L² bridge |∫ f·g| ≤ ‖f‖·‖g‖

holder_integral_abs_L2: the L² special case in Real.sqrt form, |∫ f·g dμ| ≤ √(∫ f²)·√(∫ g²), recovering the shape of the parent gallery's bunyakovsky_schwarz_abs by rewriting the 1/2-powers (Real.rpow_two / Real.sqrt_eq_rpow) at the conjugation fixed point p = q = 2

holder_recovers_cauchy_schwarz: the squared Cauchy–Schwarz integral inequality (∫ f·g)² ≤ (∫ f²)·(∫ g²) obtained purely as the p = q = 2 case of Hölder, proving the parent's bunyakovsky_schwarz_sq is not an independent theorem but the diagonal restriction of the conjugate-exponent family
holder_integral_abs_symm: the pairing bound is invariant under swapping (f, p) ↔ (g, q), reflecting the symmetry p.HolderConjugate q ↔ q.HolderConjugate p of the conjugation

description: Answers the parent open question (cauchy-schwarz-integral-oq-03): can the 'inner-product = integral' bridge that powered the L² Bunyakovsky–Schwarz inequality extend to Lᵖ for p ≠ 2? The answer is yes, and the correct generalization is Hölder's inequality. This entry proves the signed integral Hölder bound |∫ f·g dμ| ≤ (∫ |f|ᵖ)^{1/p}·(∫ |g|ᵍ)^{1/q} for real-valued f ∈ Lᵖ, g ∈ Lᵍ with conjugate exponents 1/p + 1/q = 1 (Mathlib only provides the nonnegative and norm variants), then shows the parent's L² results fall out as the single fixed point p = q = 2 of the conjugation p ↦ p/(p−1): the sqrt-form bound |∫ f·g| ≤ √(∫ f²)·√(∫ g²) and the squared Cauchy–Schwarz (∫ f·g)² ≤ (∫ f²)·(∫ g²). A symmetry theorem records the (f,p) ↔ (g,q) invariance. 4 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms.

overview.historicalContext: The L² Cauchy–Schwarz inequality works because L²(μ) is a Hilbert space that is its own dual: the pairing ⟪f,g⟫ = ∫ f·g is an inner product, so |⟪f,g⟫| ≤ ‖f‖·‖g‖ is automatic. For p ≠ 2 there is no inner product, but there is still a duality — between Lᵖ and its conjugate space Lᵍ with 1/p + 1/q = 1 — and Hölder's inequality (Otto Hölder, 1889; anticipated by Rogers, 1888) is exactly the pairing bound that realizes it. Cauchy–Schwarz is the self-dual diagonal p = q = 2, the unique fixed point of the conjugation p ↦ p/(p−1).
overview.problemStatement: The parent entry proved |∫ f·g dμ| ≤ ‖f‖_{L²}·‖g‖_{L²} by invoking the inner-product structure of L². Its open question asks whether the bridge survives when p ≠ 2, i.e. whether there is a corresponding bound pairing an Lᵖ function against an Lᵍ function, and whether the L² statement is recovered as a special case.
overview.text: Fix conjugate exponents p, q (Real.HolderConjugate p q, equivalently 1/p + 1/q = 1 with p, q > 1) and real-valued f ∈ Lᵖ(μ), g ∈ Lᵍ(μ). Then |∫ f·g dμ| ≤ (∫ |f|ᵖ dμ)^{1/p}·(∫ |g|ᵍ dμ)^{1/q}. At p = q = 2 (which is Hölder-conjugate to itself) the right side becomes √(∫ f²)·√(∫ g²) = ‖f‖_{L²}·‖g‖_{L²}, so the bound is the parent's Bunyakovsky–Schwarz inequality; squaring gives (∫ f·g)² ≤ (∫ f²)·(∫ g²). The bridge therefore extends to every p ≠ 2, with the L² inner-product case as one point of a continuum.
overview.proofStrategy: The signed bound is obtained by inserting an absolute value: |∫ f·g| ≤ ∫ |f·g| (abs_integral_le_integral_abs, which needs no integrability hypothesis) = ∫ |f|·|g| (abs_mul), then Mathlib's norm-form Hölder integral_mul_norm_le_Lp_mul_Lq applied to the ℝ-norm, where ‖x‖ = |x|. The L² specialization instantiates this at Real.HolderConjugate.two_two and converts |f|^(2:ℝ) = f² via Real.rpow_two together with sq_abs, and the 1/2-powers into square roots via Real.sqrt_eq_rpow. Squaring the sqrt-form bound with pow_le_pow_left₀ and collapsing (√A)² = A via Real.sq_sqrt yields the classical squared Cauchy–Schwarz. Symmetry is Real.HolderConjugate.symm.
keyInsights: The 'bridge' of the L² case was self-duality (an inner product); the general bridge is Lᵖ–Lᵍ duality, and Hölder's inequality is the pairing bound that makes it explicit — Cauchy–Schwarz is precisely the self-dual fixed point p = q = 2

Signedness is the only real content beyond Mathlib: the library bounds ∫ ‖f‖·‖g‖ or assumes f, g ≥ 0, but the parent bridge is about the signed pairing ∫ f·g, recovered here by |∫ f·g| ≤ ∫ |f·g| before applying the norm-form inequality

The parent's two headline theorems (absolute-value and squared Bunyakovsky–Schwarz) are not separate results but the p = q = 2 slice of a one-parameter family; the sqrt-form bound literally is ‖f‖_{L²}·‖g‖_{L²} once (∫ f²)^{1/2} is read as the L² norm
The bound is symmetric under (f, p) ↔ (g, q) because conjugacy is symmetric — the same reason ∫ f·g pairs Lᵖ with Lᵍ rather than distinguishing a preferred factor

The signed-reduction step |∫ f·g| ≤ ∫ |f·g| (abs_integral_le_integral_abs) costs nothing extra in hypotheses: Mathlib's Bochner integral defaults to 0 on non-integrable functions, so the inequality holds unconditionally, before f·g ∈ L¹ is ever established — the MemLp f p / MemLp g q hypotheses only need to feed the norm-form Hölder step that follows
prerequisites: The L² Bunyakovsky–Schwarz inequality and its inner-product proof (parent entry cauchy-schwarz-integral)
Conjugate (Hölder) exponents 1/p + 1/q = 1 and the self-conjugacy of 2 (Real.HolderConjugate, two_two)
Mathlib's norm-form integral Hölder inequality integral_mul_norm_le_Lp_mul_Lq and MemLp membership
Basic real-power identities: Real.rpow_two, Real.sqrt_eq_rpow, Real.sq_sqrt

sections.title: Recovering squared Cauchy–Schwarz
sections.summary: holder_recovers_cauchy_schwarz: (∫ f·g)² ≤ (∫ f²)·(∫ g²). Squares the sqrt-form bound (pow_le_pow_left₀ on the nonnegative sides, sq_abs) and collapses (√A)² = A via Real.sq_sqrt, exhibiting the parent's bunyakovsky_schwarz_sq as the diagonal of Hölder.

sections.title: Symmetry of the pairing bound
sections.summary: holder_integral_abs_symm: swapping (f, p) ↔ (g, q) preserves the inequality, an immediate consequence of Real.HolderConjugate.symm and the symmetry of ∫ f·g.
sections.mathContext: $p \ \text{conj}\ q \iff q\ \text{conj}\ p$; bound invariant under swap.

conclusion.summary: The L² Bunyakovsky–Schwarz bridge extends to every conjugate exponent pair via Hölder's inequality: for real f ∈ Lᵖ and g ∈ Lᵍ with 1/p + 1/q = 1, |∫ f·g dμ| ≤ (∫ |f|ᵖ)^{1/p}·(∫ |g|ᵍ)^{1/q}. The parent's L² theorems are recovered as the self-conjugate case p = q = 2: the sqrt-form bound √(∫ f²)·√(∫ g²) = ‖f‖_{L²}·‖g‖_{L²} and the squared inequality (∫ f·g)² ≤ (∫ f²)·(∫ g²). 4 theorems, 141 lines, 0 sorries, 0 axioms.
conclusion.implications: Reframes Cauchy–Schwarz as the self-dual point of a one-parameter family of pairing inequalities: the inner-product structure that made the L² proof effortless is the p = 2 specialization of Lᵖ–Lᵍ duality. The signed formulation supplies the missing piece over Mathlib's nonnegative/norm forms, matching the parent bridge's ∫ f·g exactly.
openQuestions: Package the right-hand side as toReal of eLpNorm f p · eLpNorm g q, giving a literal ‖f‖_p·‖g‖_q bridge that specializes to the L² norm and connects to Mathlib's Lᵖ space API
Prove the companion Lᵖ–Lᵍ product integrability bridge (f ∈ Lᵖ, g ∈ Lᵍ ⟹ f·g ∈ L¹) generalizing that L²·L² ⊆ L¹, and the equality/extremal case (equality iff |f|ᵖ and |g|ᵍ are proportional a.e.)

crossReferences.description: Parent entry: proved the L² Bunyakovsky–Schwarz inequality via the inner-product = integral bridge and asked (open question 3) whether the bridge extends to Lᵖ for p ≠ 2. This entry answers yes via Hölder's inequality, recovering the parent's absolute-value and squared L² theorems as the self-conjugate case p = q = 2.

Sibling under the same parent, also framing Hölder as the generalization of Cauchy–Schwarz — but in the nonnegative / norm form ∫ |f·g| ≤ (∫|f|ᵖ)^{1/p}(∫|g|ᵍ)^{1/q}. This entry supplies the complementary signed pairing bound |∫ f·g| ≤ … and additionally recovers the L² sqrt-form and squared Cauchy–Schwarz as the p = q = 2 fixed point.

The finite-dimensional / inner-product Cauchy–Schwarz inequality (abstract inner product, Lagrange identity, and finite sums). It is the discrete counterpart of the L² case recovered here as p = q = 2; the integral bound ∫ f·g ≤ ‖f‖₂‖g‖₂ is the continuum analogue of ⟨u,v⟩ ≤ ‖u‖‖v‖.

Hölder's inequality rests on convexity: the pointwise Young inequality ab ≤ aᵖ/p + bᵍ/q that underlies it is exactly the convexity (Jensen) inequality for exp, and the equality case |f|ᵖ ∝ |g|ᵍ mirrors Jensen's equality-iff-constant characterization. This entry's open question on the extremal case connects directly to that Jensen equality analysis.
